handoff.subject: Comparison of the MCP servers for Revit present on the maintainer's workstation, and what zenrvt takes from it
handoff.produced_by: orchestrated audit (one orchestrator, four static reviewers, one code reviewer, sequential dynamic checks on a SANDBOX copy)

where_the_details_are.private: the full audit report with file:line evidence stays outside this repository (maintainer's workspace); nothing in it is needed to act on this hand-off

servers.name: mcp-server-for-revit-python (pyRevit extension)
servers.state: in service, declared twice under two names on the workstation
keep_from_it: IronPython access and pyRevit-style query helpers (behaviour only, clean-room)
error hints in the run response
route-to-tool symmetry and tests without Revit
do_not_repeat: no authentication on a loopback HTTP route (cross-site request from a browser page possible)
singleton request handler shared by concurrent servers
destructive document routes (save, close, sync) without any guard

servers.name: mcp-server-for-revit (npm server + C# plugin)
servers.state: declared but dead on the workstation (plugin manifest disabled); removed from the client configuration on 2026-10-09
keep_from_it: zod-style typed schemas with units in the description
one Revit call at a time (global mutex)
do_not_repeat: raw TCP on a fixed well-known port, bound to all interfaces, no authentication, no framing
native dependency that silently kills tools when missing

servers.name: rvt-mcp (bimwright)
keep_from_it: tool annotations readOnly/destructive/idempotent driving a generated client allow-list and a --read-only mode
_changes and _history receipts on every mutating call, record_change, per-model history
survey_change_impact with an explicit scope threshold before type changes
per-instance discovery files, switch_target, structured TARGET_* errors
response size guard with file spill and *_truncated fields
baked tools: scripts frozen into compiled commands with ribbon slots after human acceptance
in-Revit activity card, history window, ribbon ON/OFF
template-centric typed tools: view templates, filters, shared parameters, schedules, sheets, materials, families, audit
C# through Roslyn in process with a failures pre-processor
no telemetry, secret masking, path sanitising
do_not_repeat: guard rails that are a convention (prompt) rather than enforced by the server
no document policy by file name, no dry-run on the most common writes, no MCP undo
session token stored in clear in a user-readable file (acceptable, but zenrvt's secret file and signed requests do better)
one client per instance with no queueing of a second client (zenrvt answers LEASE_HELD with the holder)

servers.name: zenrvt
servers.state: not connected: no listener, no MCP server process, zero tools; ribbon with Status and Probe Python only
gaps_to_close_before_any_listener: __import__ guard and closed standard-library subset (SECURITY.md promised them)
timeout invariant enforced inside Zenrvt.Scripting; except-narrowing on the AST covering KeyboardInterrupt and tuple forms
stdout/stderr bounded to 1 MiB; result_ref for results above the frame limit
installed add-in older than the timeout fix; SHA256SUMS.txt never produced by Stage
ADR-002/004/008 still written for the HTTP design
git remote not configured, CI never executed; the clean-room check would fail on two source lines that mention pyRevit

decisions.summary: zenrvt converges the typed, annotated tool surface and in-Revit experience of rvt-mcp with the Python scripting of the pyRevit extension, on top of its own authenticated transport, document policy, read guard and journal; guard rails are enforced by the server so that no client-side hook is required; C# joins Python under the same guard; the in-Revit UI (ribbon, icons, history window, visual identity working name Z#D01) is a separate work stream; milestones M3-M5 redefined; M1 and M2 unchanged.
decisions.interpretation_to_confirm_with_the_maint: "use the same principle as rvt-mcp to get past the guard rails" was read as: build the guard rails into the server (annotations, receipts, policy, generated allow-list) so that the client-side hooks and manual confirmations become unnecessary — not as removing protections.

roadmap.M1: unchanged (read-only end to end, six audit presets at parity, install claude, activity card) — plan in docs/plans/m1-read-only/
roadmap.M2: guarded writes + change receipts and record_change
roadmap.M3: typed library wave 1 (template-centric), survey, batch, read-only mode by annotation, generated allow-list, result_ref
roadmap.M4: C# (Roslyn) under the same guard, baked commands with ribbon slots, multi-instance, exports, MCP prompts
roadmap.M5: ribbon and visual identity work stream (own product/design/slice gates)
roadmap.v1.0.0: M1-M3 + installer, CI, self-tests, ADR-014 benchmark

estimates_days.M3_M4_M5: not estimated yet; to be gated one at a time (one firm commitment at a time)

next_actions_ordered.action: Close the engine gaps: __import__ guard, stdlib subset, timeout invariant in Run, AST except-narrowing, bounded stdout
Rewrite ADR-002/004/008 for the pipe transport; keep SECURITY.md and README truthful (status note added on 2026-10-09)
Produce SHA256SUMS.txt in Stage and add a freshness check (dist vs installed) to install.ps1; reinstall the add-in
Configure the git remote (private first) and run the CI once; fix the two clean-room hits
Write the M3 product gate: list of typed tools wave 1 with their annotations, adopting rvt-mcp's naming where compatible, with Apache-2.0 attribution for adapted schemas
Open the UI work stream (ribbon, icons, history window, visual identity Z#D01) with its own product gate; do not block M1-M2
Re-run the 12 scenarios against the pyRevit extension and rvt-mcp with a zenrvt build at the end of M2, then of M3; publish docs/benchmark/<date>-comparison.md

open_questions_for_the_maintainer: Exact meaning and assets of the visual identity "Z#D01" (palette, icon style, typography) — needed to open the UI work stream
Adopt rvt-mcp's public tool names verbatim (revit_<verb>_<noun>) for client-side compatibility, or zenrvt's own namespace?
Port selected rvt-mcp handlers under Apache-2.0 attribution, or re-implement from the schemas only?
Should the maintainer's private client-side hook be retired once the server-side guard rails ship, or kept as belt and braces?
